items.front: Which body recommended the Governor be a detached, non-partisan person from outside the State?
items.back: The Sarkaria Commission (1983); echoed by the Punchhi Commission.
items.examPoint: Governor — discretionary powers; Sarkaria/Punchhi & SC on assent

items.front: How is the Governor appointed and removed?
items.back: Appointed by the President (Art 155); holds office during the President's pleasure (Art 156) — no fixed removal procedure in the Constitution.

items.front: What immunities does Article 361 give the Governor?
items.back: No criminal proceedings during the term of office; emoluments cannot be diminished during the term.
items.examPoint: Governor — term, oath, qualifications & conditions of office

items.front: Key discretionary powers of the Governor?
items.back: Reserving a bill for the President (Art 200), recommending President's Rule (Art 356 report), and choosing a CM in a hung assembly.
items.examPoint: Governor — discretionary powers; Sarkaria/Punchhi & SC on assent

items.front: How is the Chief Secretary appointed, and is the post fixed-tenure?
items.back: Appointed by the CM (not the Governor); it is NOT a fixed-tenure post.

items.front: Maximum size and minimum size of a Legislative Council?
items.back: Not more than one-third of the Assembly's strength, and not less than 40 (Art 171).
items.examPoint: Legislative Council — composition (Art 171); 5/6 elected, 1/6 nominated; permanent body

items.front: Who elects the Chairman of the Legislative Council?
items.back: The members of the Council elect their Chairman (the Governor does NOT nominate the Chairman).
items.examPoint: Legislative Council — composition (Art 171); 5/6 elected, 1/6 nominated; permanent body

items.front: Does the Speaker of the Assembly vacate office on its dissolution?
items.back: No — the Speaker continues until immediately before the first meeting of the new Assembly. He vacates only if he ceases to be a member.

items.front: Council composition (Art 171) — elected vs nominated shares?
items.back: 1/3 by local bodies, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/6 nominated by Governor → 5/6 elected, 1/6 nominated.
items.examPoint: Legislative Council — composition (Art 171); 5/6 elected, 1/6 nominated; permanent body

items.front: Creation or abolition of a Legislative Council — which Article and process?
items.back: Article 169 — Parliament by law, on a special-majority resolution of the Assembly (treated as ordinary law, not an Art 368 amendment).
items.examPoint: Creation & abolition of Legislative Council — Article 169

items.front: Non-legislator as a State minister — for how long?
items.back: Maximum six months (Art 164(4)); a member disqualified for defection cannot be a minister (91st Amd).

items.front: Not a necessary consequence of President's Rule (Art 356) in a State?
items.back: Dissolution of the Assembly (it may just be suspended) and dissolution of local bodies (unaffected). CoM is always dismissed.
items.examPoint: State Legislature — money bill, legislative process, control over executive

items.front: AP legislature — Assembly and Council strength?
items.back: Bicameral at Amaravati: Assembly 175 seats; Legislative Council 58 seats. AP Council: abolished 1985, revived 2007 (Art 169).
items.examPoint: AP angle — Assembly strength 175, Council 58 seats, bicameral

items.front: AP CM and Governor as of Sep 2026?
items.back: CM: N. Chandrababu Naidu (Kuppam; 4th term since 12 Jun 2024). Governor: Justice (Retd) S. Abdul Nazeer (since 24 Feb 2023).
items.examPoint: AP executive — CM N. Chandrababu Naidu (Kuppam), 4th term since 12 Jun 2024

items.front: Who appoints the Chief Secretary of a State, and is the tenure fixed?
items.back: The Chief Minister appoints the Chief Secretary (administrative head of the State secretariat); the post has no fixed statutory tenure.
items.examPoint: Chief Secretary — appointment by CM, no fixed tenure

items.back: During the term of office the Governor is not answerable to any court, and no criminal proceedings can be instituted or continued against him/her.

items.front: What happens to the Assembly Speaker on dissolution?
items.back: The Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution; he continues until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Assembly.
items.examPoint: Speaker of Assembly continues after dissolution
